passage.text: Marie Curie is a famous name in science.
passage.reading: məˈriː ˈkjʊri ɪz ə ˈfeɪməs ˈneɪm ɪn ˈsaɪəns.

passage.text: She came from Poland, but she studied and worked in Paris.
passage.reading: ʃiː ˈkeɪm frəm ˈpoʊlənd, bʌt ʃiː ˈstʌdid ənd ˈwɜːrkt ɪn ˈpɛrɪs.

passage.text: At that time, very few women went to university.
passage.reading: ət ðæt ˈtaɪm, ˈvɛri ˈfjuː ˈwɪmɪn ˈwɛnt tə ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːrsəti.

passage.text: In Paris, she met Pierre Curie, a scientist, and they got married in 1895.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈpɛrɪs, ʃiː ˈmɛt piˈɛr ˈkjʊri, ə ˈsaɪəntɪst, ənd ðeɪ ˈɡɑːt ˈmærid ɪn ˌeɪˈtiːn ˈnaɪnti ˈfaɪv.
təˈɡɛðər, ðeɪ dɪˈskʌvərd ˈreɪdiəm ɪn ˌeɪˈtiːn ˈnaɪnti ˈeɪt.

passage.text: Later, doctors used it to help very sick people.
passage.reading: ˈleɪtər, ˈdɑːktərz ˈjuːzd ɪt tə ˈhɛlp ˈvɛri ˈsɪk ˈpiːpəl.

passage.text: In 1903, they won the Nobel Prize in Physics.
passage.reading: ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈoʊ ˈθriː, ðeɪ ˈwʌn ðə noʊˈbɛl ˈpraɪz ɪn ˈfɪzɪks.

passage.text: She was the first female scientist who won a Nobel Prize.
passage.reading: ʃiː wʌz ðə ˈfɜːrst ˈfiːmeɪl ˈsaɪəntɪst huː ˈwʌn ə noʊˈbɛl ˈpraɪz.

passage.text: Sadly, Pierre lost his life in a street accident in 1906.
passage.reading: ˈsædli, piˈɛr ˈlɔːst hɪz ˈlaɪf ɪn ə ˈstriːt ˈæksɪdənt ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈoʊ ˈsɪks.

passage.text: Marie was very sad, but she did not stop working.
passage.reading: məˈriː wʌz ˈvɛri ˈsæd, bʌt ʃiː dɪd ˈnɑːt ˈstɑːp ˈwɜːrkɪŋ.

passage.text: In 1911, she won a second Nobel Prize, this time in chemistry.
passage.reading: ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ɪˈlɛvən, ʃiː ˈwʌn ə ˈsɛkənd noʊˈbɛl ˈpraɪz, ˈðɪs ˈtaɪm ɪn ˈkɛmɪstri.

passage.text: Today, she is still the only person with Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
passage.reading: təˈdeɪ, ʃiː ɪz ˈstɪl ði ˈoʊnli ˈpɜːrsən wɪð noʊˈbɛl ˈpraɪzɪz ɪn ˈtuː ˈdɪfərənt ˈsaɪənsɪz.

passage.text: Her achievements changed medicine, and doctors still use her ideas in hospitals today.
passage.reading: hɜːr əˈtʃiːvmənts ˈtʃeɪndʒd ˈmɛdəsən, ənd ˈdɑːktərz ˈstɪl ˈjuːz hɜːr aɪˈdiːəz ɪn ˈhɑːspɪtəlz təˈdeɪ.

passage.text: She showed the world that a female scientist could be as great as any man.
passage.reading: ʃiː ˈʃoʊd ðə ˈwɜːrld ðæt ə ˈfiːmeɪl ˈsaɪəntɪst kʊd bi əz ˈɡreɪt əz ˈɛni ˈmæn.
